about: The core's neutral error classes (ADR 0019). A target maps its runtime's failures to these names and the details each takes; a source maps each class to its own codes, messages and severities. A class speaks of the failure, never of a runtime. A failure no target maps to a class, or a class no source covers, gets the source's reserved code and is flagged. A new class is added by the ticket that builds the behaviour that raises it, with its entries in both halves and a case in tests/error_cases.py.

classes.name: divide_by_zero
classes.meaning: A division or a remainder had a divisor of zero.

classes.name: arithmetic_overflow
classes.meaning: A result of arithmetic, or a value converted to another number type, does not fit the type it must take.

details.name: to_type
details.meaning: The vocabulary type the value had to fit, by name: an integer with its bits and sign, such as integer(32, signed), and any other type by its name alone, such as decimal.

details.name: from_type
details.meaning: The vocabulary type of the value converted, when the code that converts knows it; a target's runtime does not say.

classes.name: conversion_failure
classes.meaning: A text could not be converted to a number type.

details.name: to_type
details.meaning: The vocabulary type the value had to fit, by name: an integer with its bits and sign, such as integer(32, signed), and any other type by its name alone, such as decimal.

details.name: from_type
details.meaning: The vocabulary type of the text, such as string(bytes) or string(utf16), when the code that converts knows it; a target's runtime does not say.

classes.name: datetime_conversion_failure
classes.meaning: A text could not be converted to a date or a time.

classes.name: scalar_subquery_multiple_rows
classes.meaning: A query used as a single value returned more than one row.

classes.name: not_null_violation
classes.meaning: A null was written to a column that does not allow nulls.

details.name: table
details.meaning: The table, qualified by database and schema.

details.name: verb
details.meaning: The write that failed: INSERT or UPDATE.

classes.name: check_violation
classes.meaning: A written row broke a check constraint.

details.name: verb
details.meaning: The write that failed: INSERT or UPDATE.

details.name: column
details.meaning: The column the constraint is on, when it is on exactly one.

classes.name: foreign_key_violation
classes.meaning: A write left a foreign key without its parent row: a child written with no parent, or a parent changed or removed while a child still refers to it.

details.name: kind
details.meaning: FOREIGN KEY when the child is written; REFERENCE when the parent is changed; SAME TABLE REFERENCE when the table refers to itself.

details.name: verb
details.meaning: The write that failed: INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE.

details.name: database
details.meaning: The database of the table named.

details.name: table
details.meaning: The table named, qualified by schema.

details.name: column
details.meaning: The first column of the key on that table.

classes.name: primary_key_violation
classes.meaning: A write would give two rows the same primary key.

details.name: key
details.meaning: The duplicate key value, written as the source writes a key.

classes.name: unique_constraint_violation
classes.meaning: A write would give two rows the same value under a unique constraint.

details.name: key
details.meaning: The duplicate key value, written as the source writes a key.

classes.name: unique_index_violation
classes.meaning: A write would give two rows the same value under a unique index.

details.name: key
details.meaning: The duplicate key value, written as the source writes a key.

classes.name: object_not_found
classes.meaning: A statement named a table, view or other object that does not exist. Found when the statement runs, not before: the code around it has already begun.

details.name: name
details.meaning: The name as the statement wrote it.

classes.name: column_not_found
classes.meaning: A statement named a column that does not exist. Found when the statement runs, not before.

details.name: name
details.meaning: The name as the statement wrote it.

classes.name: object_already_exists
classes.meaning: A statement created an object under a name already taken.

classes.name: drop_target_not_found
classes.meaning: A statement dropped an object that does not exist.

classes.name: identity_insert_not_allowed
classes.meaning: A value was written explicitly to a column the system numbers, while explicit writes to it are off.

classes.name: identity_update_not_allowed
classes.meaning: An update changed a column the system numbers.

classes.name: nesting_level_exceeded
classes.meaning: Procedures, functions, triggers or views called one another more deeply than the limit.

classes.name: transaction_request_without_begin
classes.meaning: A commit, a rollback or a savepoint was requested while no transaction was open.

classes.name: savepoint_not_found
classes.meaning: A rollback named a savepoint or a transaction that is not open.

classes.name: transaction_count_mismatch
classes.meaning: A procedure ended with a different number of transactions open than it began with: it opened one it did not close, or closed more than it opened. The caller goes on.

details.name: previous
details.meaning: The number of transactions open when the procedure was called.

details.name: current
details.meaning: The number open when it ended.

classes.name: raised_error
classes.meaning: The code raised an error of its own at a severity that transfers control to a handler, and processing goes on after it unless the setting that aborts on error is on. Number, message, severity and state are the code's.

classes.name: thrown_error
classes.meaning: The code raised an error of its own in the form that ends the batch. Number, message and state are the code's; the severity is fixed.

details.name: number
details.meaning: The error number the code gave.

classes.name: throw_number_out_of_range
classes.meaning: The code raised an error of its own with a number outside the range reserved for the code's own errors.

classes.name: raise_severity_not_permitted
classes.meaning: The code raised an error of its own at a severity reserved for the system.

classes.name: raise_format_invalid
classes.meaning: The message text of an error the code raised holds a placeholder that is not valid.

classes.name: raise_argument_mismatch
classes.meaning: A value given for a placeholder of an error message is not of the type the placeholder takes.

details.name: index
details.meaning: The position of the value, counting from 1.
